title: Shared memory parallelism in Julia | Kiran Pamnany | Cambridge Julia Meetup (May 2018)
summary: Kiran Pamnany's Cambridge Julia Meetup talk on Julia's shared memory parallelism and its new task scheduler. It argues that fork-join and work-stealing models nest poorly and presents depth-first scheduling for composable parallelism.
why: Recommended in Julia threading threads as an insightful, simple explanation of the new task scheduler.

quote.text: I found his talk to be an insightful overview of this work
